newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tighter Danish fiscal policy needed in 98 - banker.
newsitem.headline: Tighter Danish fiscal policy needed in 98 - banker.

text.p: Den Danske Bank, Denmark's biggest, on Wednesday added its voice to calls for fiscal tightening in 1998, saying suggestions from the country's Independent Economic Council did not go far enough.
"The government will have to tighten finance policy much more than the figure mentioned in the Wise Men's report," Joergen Birger Christensen, chief economist at Den Danske Bank told Reuters.

Earlier Denmark's Economic Council, known as the Wise Men, said in a biannual report that the economy needed extra fiscal tightening equal to about 0.4 percent of GDP or four billion crowns ($626 million) to prevent overheating next year.

Christensen said that such a move would only have a neutral effect on finance policy in 1998. He reckoned that a further five to six billion crowns in fiscal tightening would be needed to achieve the 0.5 percent target.
Economy Minister Marianne Jelved said earlier on Wednesday that the government would take enough measures to have an effect.
"The government intends to tighten fiscal policy in 1998 by more than the four billion crowns mentioned in the Economic Council report," she told Reuters.

"The government has stated that it intends to continue its fiscal tightening policies into 1998. By that we do not mean that our fiscal policy will be neutral but that it will be tightened," she said. "It is too early though to say now just how big the tightening will be," Jelved added.
